# Draft:Speaking likeness

The speaking likeness was a genre of Renaissance sculpture and painting that sought to capture momentary motions or expressions indicative of a subject speaking or preparing to speak. The style was popularized by Italian sculptor Gian Lorenzo Bernini, particularly in his biographic works.
Hill, Michael. 1998. “Cardinal Dying: Bernini’s Bust of Scipione Borghese.” Australian Journal of Art 14 (1): 9–24. doi:10.1080/03146464.1998.11432850.
